title: Code Review Checklist
summary: Master Code Review Checklist through explanation, prediction, implementation, and review.

challenges.title: Recall checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Without reopening the lesson, explain Code Review Checklist in your own words. Include the problem it solves, the core mechanism, and one boundary or failure.
challenges.hint: Use “Intent” as a cue, then close the lesson again.

challenges.title: Prediction checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Choose one example or source file from this mission. Predict its behavior for a normal input and a changed or invalid input before running or revealing the reference. Explain the rule separating the outcomes.
challenges.hint: Change one condition at a time so the result teaches a rule.

challenges.title: Build and prove checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Implement, debug, or adapt the mission exercise yourself. Record the acceptance criterion, command or interaction used to verify it, failure evidence, and one tradeoff. Do not paste the reference solution.
challenges.hint: A passing check, measured result, focused diff, or reproducible demo is stronger than ‘done.’

files.content:
# Code Review Checklist

Review behavior and risk before style.

## Intent

- [ ] The change solves the stated problem and respects non-goals.
- [ ] Acceptance criteria are observable and covered.
- [ ] Complexity is proportional to the current requirement.

## Correctness

- [ ] Boundary inputs, empty states, and error paths are deliberate.
- [ ] State transitions and invariants are explicit.
- [ ] Async work handles ordering, cancellation, timeout, and cleanup.
- [ ] Concurrent or duplicate operations cannot silently corrupt state.
- [ ] Time, randomness, filesystem, network, and database behavior are testable.

## Data and API

- [ ] Runtime input is validated even when compile-time types exist.
- [ ] Database constraints reinforce durable invariants.
- [ ] Queries avoid unnecessary round trips and unbounded results.
- [ ] HTTP status, error shape, pagination, and compatibility are consistent.
- [ ] Migrations have deploy-order and rollback/roll-forward consideration.

## Security

- [ ] Authentication and resource-level authorization are separate and tested.
- [ ] User-controlled data cannot become code, markup, query, or log structure.
- [ ] Secrets and sensitive fields are absent from code, errors, and logs.
- [ ] Abuse, replay, enumeration, and resource exhaustion were considered.

## Tests

- [ ] Tests protect behavior rather than implementation details.
- [ ] A regression test fails before the fix.
- [ ] Fixtures are deterministic and isolated.
- [ ] Cleanup is awaited and leaves no open handles.
- [ ] Skips and retries are visible and justified.

## Operations

- [ ] Failures are diagnosable through stable log/metric/trace fields.
- [ ] Health signals reflect real dependency readiness.
- [ ] Rollout and recovery do not require hidden knowledge.
- [ ] Performance claims include measurements and context.

## Communication

- [ ] Names and comments explain intent rather than restate syntax.
- [ ] Documentation and examples changed with the contract.
- [ ] The PR is small enough to review confidently.

Finish with prioritized comments: blocking correctness/security issues first,
then maintainability, then optional suggestions. Explain the failure scenario,
not merely the preferred code style.
